description: A long question, a prayer of several paragraphs pasted in beside the question, is read whole: the cleaned question keeps every paragraph, to its last words, and is not cut at the first line.

request.greek: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν τὸν θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν
request.english: And we know that all things work together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
request.question:
What does Paul teach about prayer here? Here is my own prayer for context:

Lord, my Father, I come to you at the end of this day. Guard me against envy, pride and anger, and keep me from the small lies I tell to look better than I am.

Teach me to love the people you have put near me, the ones who are easy and the ones who wear me out. Give me patience with my family, honesty with my friends, and mercy toward those who have wronged me, as you have been merciful to me.

When I read your word, open my eyes. Let me not read it to win an argument or to feel clever, but to know you. Make me quiet enough to hear, humble enough to obey, and glad enough to sing.

Forgive me for what I did today and for what I left undone. Forgive me for the hours I wasted and the words I should not have said. Wash me and begin again with me, because I have no other hope than your kindness.

Keep those I love, wherever they are tonight. Be near the sick and the lonely and those who cannot sleep for fear. Let your peace guard my heart and my mind, and let me wake tomorrow ready to walk in your way. Amen.

question.contains: let me wake tomorrow ready to walk in your way. Amen.
